<div  class="content">
                                                                        <div  style="width: 100%; overflow: hidden;" class="topBanner">
                        <img fetchpriority="high" style="width: 100%;" src="https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/732d7c_93b681c85ddb45c493ea7cc561dc1cc4_mv2_d_2048_1365_s_2-2.png" alt="" class="banner-img"/>                        <div  class="positioned">
                            <h1>Turks and Caicos Kiteboarding</h1>
                                                            <article>
                                    <p>Perfect ocean conditions, no breaking waves, no hazards and constant on-shore breeze.​ Villa Esencia has an especially easy and safe environment to learn kiting.</p>
                                    <a href="#">learn to kite with the pros</a>
                                </article>
                                                    </div>
                    </div>                           
                <div  class="info-section left">
                                    <div  class="info-section-box">
                    <div class="imgItem "  style="background-image: url('https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/732d7c_9e1cfe801b6149e4b09f744df87e74de_mv2_d_3931_2946_s_4_2.png');">
                                            </div>
                    <div class="itemText">
                        <article>
                        <h3>Shallow Sea</h3>
                        <p>You can stand up and walk a long ways out. If you get tired or lose your board you can simply stand up and walk to it. Trying to learn kiting in deep water adds a whole level of unnecessary difficulty. Also here there are no strong currents.</p>
                                                </article>
                    </div> 
                </div>
                            <div  class="info-section-box">
                    <div class="imgItem "  style="background-image: url('https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/732d7c_9f0a7d0cc0c0458da91e51436923ca51_mv2_d_4608_3072_s_4_2.png');">
                                            </div>
                    <div class="itemText">
                        <article>
                        <h3>Warm Waters</h3>
                        <p>It’s great to be able to spend hours in the water without getting cold - and that’s without a wetsuit. The Caribbean sea is generally warm anyway and the Caicos Bank that we are on, being shallow, heats up even more.</p>
                                                </article>
                    </div> 
                </div>
                            <div  class="info-section-box">
                    <div class="imgItem "  style="background-image: url('https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/732d7c_9e1cfe801b6149e4b09f744df87e74de_mv2_d_3931_2946_s_4_2.png');">
                                            </div>
                    <div class="itemText">
                        <article>
                        <h3>Gentle & Safe</h3>
                        <p>The sandy beach has no rocks or large projecting sharp objects. The side/on shore winds will always bring you back to the beach. The shallow waters mean you can always stand up if you get tired or lose your board. The beach is 3+ miles of white sand and buildings are set back about 100 ft or so, so even if you crash your kite on the beach, there are no dangerous objects to entangle with (cars, buildings, etc.)</p>
                                                </article>
                    </div> 
                </div>
<style></style>
<script></script>
</div><div  class="best-kiting">
    <h2>the best kiting overall</h2>
    <div  class="flex-container">
        <div class="item">
            <article>   
                <h3>why long bay?</h3> 
                <hr />
                                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>3-mile long white sand beach </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>No rocks or jetties </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Nothing dangerous out there!</p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>The right direction of the wind - side on-shore </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Stunning clear turquoise blue water </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>No booties needed </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Right strength of wind, no big gusts</p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Winds almost all year round (Kiting season - early October until end of August) </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Warm waters </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Shallow waters - you can stand up</p>
            </article>
        </div>
        <div class="item">
            <article>   
                <h3>why esencia for kiters?</h3> 
                <hr />
                                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>The natural ambience and the beach environment </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Shade directly on the beach - Tiki huts, umbrellas, palm trees </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Comfortable lounge chairs with cushions, regular chairs, hammocks </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Daily cleaned beach </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>You are only seconds walk from your suite </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>SUP boards and ocean kayaks for no-wind days </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Great for family members who don’t kite as well as small children </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Only a few kiters! No crowds.</p>
            </article>
        </div>
        <div class="item">
            <article>   
                <h3>set-up for kiters</h3> 
                <hr />

                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Compressed air directly on the beach </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Self-launch and landing x 2 (1 on beach, 1 in the water) </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Clean, white sand launch/landing area </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Safe - you can leave your gear on the beach </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Gear storage directly off the beach </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Experienced kiters who can help you out </p>
                                            <p><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Misc. support - screws, bindings, tools, etc.</p>

<style></style>
<section data-wpr-lazyrender="1" class="ease_of_use">
	<h2 class="boxtitle">ease of use</h2>
	<p>In addition to the natural environment, we have added some ‘ease of use’ facilities on the beach to make the kiting experience more pleasurable.</p>
	<div  class="flex_wrapper">
				    		        <div class="item">
		        	<a href="#">
						<img src="https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Group-1527.png" alt="">
						<h3>COMPRESSOR</h3>
						<p>As lazy aging kiters, we’ve installed compressed air directly on the beach with fittings for most kites. Takes the back strain out of kiting and makes for a quick inflation. Simply plug in the hose to your kite, turn the valve and… done!</p>
					</a>
				</div>
		    		        <div class="item">
		        	<a href="#">
						<img src="https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Group-1528.png" alt="">
						<h3>SELF-LAUNCH AND LANDING</h3>
						<p>We have two self-launch/landing pads; one directly on the beach and one in the water. To launch your kite, you run your lines and attach the chicken loop to the launch. Then you walk to your kite and place it in the launch position in the wind window. The kite will simply sit in that position. You then walk back to the launch, hook the chicken loop to your harness, disconnect from the launch and then bring the kite up in... Read More the air. Landing is exactly the reverse. With the kite directly overhead, hook your chicken loop to the launch. Then lower the kite down to the beach. The kite will simply sit there at the end of your lines. Disconnect from the kite, walk over to it and place it down on the beach. Then return to the launch and disconnect the lines.</p>
					</a>
				</div>
		    		        <div class="item">
		        	<a href="#">
						<img src="https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Group-1529.png" alt="">
						<h3>EXTRA GEAR</h3>
						<p>We have large light wind and beginner boards here if you need them. Though we’d all like to be on a short performance board, having a big board for learning makes a great difference to ease of learning. And when the wind is light, even the advanced kiters use the bigger boards – at least you’re out on the water, and you’d be surprised what kinds of tricks you can do riding a door!</p>
					</a>
				</div>
		    		        <div class="item">
		        	<a href="#">
						<img src="https://www.villaesencia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Group-1530.png" alt="">
						<h3>ADVANCED KITING</h3>
						<p>Provo offers two types of waters for advanced kiting. Long Bay is generally flat water with some chop depending upon wind conditions. Many advanced kiters come here to work on tricks. Grace Bay (depending upon wind conditions) has a reef leading to the open sea. The reef offers wave riding and the conditions on Grace Bay are generally wilder, larger swells, waves and then open ocean.</p>
					</a>
				</div>
		    			</div>
	<style></style>
